ruling.explanation: To the rider: your claim is partly upheld. The route deviation is established on this trip's own telemetry. The governing figure is the GPS trace (27.18 km), not the 27.2 km rounded copy on the trip record, measured against the booked optimal of 21.0 km — an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.4%. That clears both of POL-RD-01's establishment tests (more than 0.8 km and more than 20% of optimal). The driver's own in-app message ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') confirms the wrong turn, and the trace itself is clean (229 fixes, 10-second sampling, no gaps), so it is not a POL-RD-07 impaired-trace case. No exculpatory clause applies: there was no traffic advisory for the AYE/MCE/ECP corridor (that artifact is missing, weight 0.0 — its absence is citable but it exonerates nothing), you requested no detour, no pickup or dropoff point was amended, and this was not a pooled trip. The refund is therefore arithmetic under POL-RD-02 on a METERED fare: charged_total = SGD 35.64; recomputed_fare = SGD 27.63, computed as (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 26.0) x surge 1.0 (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, surcharge or waiting fee; refund = SGD 8.01, rounded up to SGD 8.05. That is below 90% of the charge, so it is a partial refund rather than the full refund you asked for, and it is below the SGD 10.00 you contested. To the driver: the deviation is not MATERIAL — 6.18 km and 29.4% are both below the 8.0 km and 50% materiality gates — so no driver_profile check, no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral arise, and your record (0 deviation flags in 90 days) shows no repeat pattern in any event. There is no phantom or off-route charge in the fare, so no billing-integrity finding and no referral. The SGD 35.64 charge stands except for the SGD 8.05 returned to the rider.
